title: Memory Ordering
goal: Understand how memory orderings control instruction reordering across threads.

sections.text: CPUs and compilers reorder memory instructions for performance. Memory orderings in Rust define which reorderings are forbidden across threads.

sections.caption: The Ordering enum lives in std::sync::atomic.

sections.text: `Ordering::Relaxed` guarantees atomic read or write, but imposes no memory ordering constraints relative to other memory operations.
`Ordering::Release` on a store operation ensures all preceding memory writes become visible to another thread when it performs an `Ordering::Acquire` load.

sections.caption: Release store pairs with Acquire load to synchronize memory.

sections.text: `Ordering::SeqCst` enforces sequential consistency globally across all threads, but carries higher runtime cost on architectures like ARM.

explanation: Understand how memory orderings control instruction reordering across threads.
